item.title: Open source has a growing problem with LLM generated issues
item.description:
📝 My personal opinion is we shouldn't accept anything LLM-generated, but this is probably not the common position of most @opencontainers/runc-maintainers, so we should probably consider LLM-generated code and issues separately. IMHO, we should close all LLM-generated issues as spam, because even if they are describing real issues the entire issue description contains so much unneeded (and probably incorrect) information that it'd be better if they just provided their LLM prompt as an issue instead. , they understand what their patch does and was able to write the code themselves).

item.title: Protect Your Consciousness from AI
item.description:
📝 On social media, people are using LLMs to generate posts just for impressions, instead of going through the process of finding sources and creating authentic content themselves. I want to bring back authentic forum posts, where people can share their ideas and thoughts, with less algorithmic influence than platforms like X. LLMs can be prompted into agreeing with you, which is less likely than with a licensed therapist - it's important to have human to human feedback.
🔗 Read more: https://jordangoodman.bearblog.dev/protect-your-consciousness-from-ai/

item.title: Ask HN: How do you get over the fear of sharing code?
item.description:
📝 All my repos are private just because I worry about other students being lazy and just ripping my hard work and claiming it as their own. That really pisses me off when I hear some horror stories like that. It's obviously easier for viewers to just see public code repos and browse without ever requesting access so I know I'm losing some traffic (from my portfolio site)I was thinking the alternative would be just linking my demo on my portfolio site as a proof of concept that yes I made it, yes it works, and if you're curious , here's a link to the code u can request independently of github.
🔗 Read more: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45867176

item.title: Marble Fountain
item.description:
📝 TracksMy initial system came together quickly. My first draft was just subtracting a tube from the solid support structure which worked but was super limited. Each support:Pulls towards other supports, weighted by distance and similarity in sizeRepels away from other supportsPulls to stay in the bounding boxPulls towards a fixed radius from the center of the structureSupports also have inertia, which is where the arcs in the structure of the support columns come from.
